newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa mulls five bln rand spending cut - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa mulls five bln rand spending cut - paper.

text.p: The South African government is considering cancelling about five billion rand in unspent funds rolled over from previous fiscal years as a means of keeping a lid on the budget deficit, Business Day newspaper said on Tuesday.

Quoting an unnamed source, the paper said the finance department's decision to cancel some spending was taken after it emerged that the total amount of unspent funds from the 1994/95 fiscal year (April-March) was some 12.5 billion rand.
In the last budget the government had assumed a rollover of unspent funds into 1996/97 of around 6.4 billion rand, but it is now clear that almost double that amount was not spent.
"The department estimates that about five billion rand of the rollovers will not be allocated again," the source said.

The move to cancel spending by not re-allocating rollovers could help the government end the present fiscal year with a deficit below five percent of GDP and ease the way towards achieving the target of a four percent deficit in 1997/98.
The current official estimate for the deficit in 1996/97 is 5.1 percent.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said in June he aimed to reduce the budget deficit to four percent in 1997/98 and get it down to three percent by 1999/2000 as part of a wide-ranging macro-economic strategy to boost growth.
